messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Portuguese, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Portuguese line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
124 pois aquele imperador que lá em cima reina, 125 porque eu fui rebelde à sua lei, 126 não quer que alguém venha à sua cidade por mim.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

| Source Word | Contextual Definition (from Step 1) | Target Word / Phrase (PT) | Back‑Translation (EN) | Status | |-------------|--------------------------------------|---------------------------|------------------------|--------| | **ché** | causal conjunction “because” | **pois** | because | OK | | **quello** | demonstrative “that” (emphatic) | **aquele** | that | OK | | **imperador** | noun “Emperor” | **imperador** | Emperor | OK | | **che** | relative pronoun “who/that” | **que** | who/that | OK | | **là** | adverb of place “there” | **lá** | there | OK | | **sù** | adverb of direction “above/up” | **em cima** | up / above | OK | | **regna** | verb “reigns” (present) | **reina** | reigns | OK | | **perch'** | causal conjunction “because” | **porque** | because | OK | | **i'** | 1st‑person pronoun “I” | **eu** | I | OK | | **fu'** | copular past “was” | **fui** | was | OK | | **ribellante** | adjective “rebellious” | **rebelde** | rebellious | OK | | **a** | preposition “to” (target of rebellion) | **à** | to (the) | OK | | **la** | definite article “the” (part of *la sua legge*) | — *(omitted)* | the | **UNNECESSARY** (article not required in PT) | | **sua** | possessive adjective “his” | **sua** | his | OK | | **legge** | noun “law” | **lei** | law | OK | | **non** | negation “not” | **não** | not | OK | | **vuol** | volitional verb “wills / wants” | **quer** | wants | OK | | **che** | complementiser “that” (introducing content clause) | **que** | that | OK | | **'n** | preposition “in / into” | **à** | to (the) | OK | | **sua** | possessive adjective “his” | **sua** | his | OK | | **città** | noun “city” | **cidade** | city | OK | | **per** | preposition “through” (means) | **por** | through / by | OK | | **me** | pronoun “me” (object) | **mim** | me | OK | | **si** | impersonal reflexive pronoun “one” | **alguém** | someone | OK | | **vegna** | subjunctive verb “should come” | **venha** | should come | OK |

### Items Requiring Attention - **UNNECESSARY:** *la* – the definite article is naturally omitted in Portuguese when the possessive adjective (*sua*) is present. All other source tokens are accounted for with correct meaning and grammar.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Portuguese text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).
